claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to understand your situation better. **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand more about your situation.

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or towards his accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out with his upkeep - I contribute towards things like clothes and other expenses for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to know more details about your contributions:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand:

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (such as his mum or another person)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with his mum, not with you
- You contribute approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child. You're usually considered responsible if you either live with the child OR you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep.

The current Child Benefit rate for the eldest or only child is £25.60 per week (and £16.95 for additional children). Since you're contributing about £26 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit amount, you meet the contribution threshold.

Additionally, when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to get Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks if you contribute to the child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment - which you are doing.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet the eligibility criteria because:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're making sufficient contributions (£26 per week) towards his upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit amount
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Just be aware that if your individual income (or your partner's) exceeds £60,000 per year, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
